title: ITR Login Password Reset: Alternatives Without Aadhaar OTP
description: If you've forgotten your Income Tax e-filing portal password, several methods allow you to reset it. You can regain access even if you don't have your Aadhaar.

faq.q: Can I reset my ITR password if I don't have my PAN?
faq.a: No, your PAN is your primary identifier on the Income Tax e-filing portal, and it's essential for any password reset process. You must know your PAN to proceed.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to link Aadhaar with PAN for password reset?
faq.a: While linking Aadhaar with PAN is mandatory for filing ITRs, it's not the *only* way to reset your password. As discussed, alternatives like Net Banking, DSC, or e-filing registered OTP exist.

faq.q: What if my registered email ID and mobile number on the e-filing portal are also old?
faq.a: If both your registered email and mobile are outdated and you don't have access to Net Banking or a DSC, you might need to contact the Income Tax Department's e-filing helpdesk for assistance. This usually involves a more manual verification process.

faq.q: How long does it take to reset the password using these alternative methods?
faq.a: The process is usually instant for methods like Net Banking, DSC, or an OTP to your registered email/mobile. Once verified, you can set a new password immediately.

faq.q: Is using Net Banking for password reset secure?
faq.a: Yes, using Net Banking is considered highly secure as it leverages your bank's robust authentication mechanisms. Your identity is verified by the bank before you are redirected to the e-filing portal.

faq.q: Can NRIs use these methods to reset their ITR password?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can also use these methods, provided they have an Indian bank account with Net Banking access, a registered DSC in India, or access to the email/mobile number registered on their e-filing profile.

faq.q: What is a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?
faq.a: A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is an electronic form of a physical or paper certificate. It serves as proof of identity of an individual or organisation for various online transactions and is legally valid under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
